newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov sees lower electricity rates soon.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov sees lower electricity rates soon.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov hopes to announce lower electricity tariffs for industry soon, part of a sweeping campaign to reform the electricity monopoly, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

"Economic growth for Russia equals conserving and strengthening UES plus lowering electricity tariffs, all through competition between electricity generating stations and the attraction of investment in energy," Nemtsov said, referring to Unified Energy System , the power monopoly.
He was also quoted as saying that new, lower tariffs could come into effect as early as this summer and that barter payments and crime in the sector had to be rooted out.
Nemtsov, a market-oriented reformer, is in charge of revamping Russia's natural monopolies to make them more competitive and to offer supplies reflecting costs.
But he has said many times that UES, as well as natural gas monopoly Gazprom, will not be broken up.

While average Russian electricity tariffs are much lower than those in the West, according to brokerage Troika Dialog, prices for industrial firms are higher than household rates -- the opposite of the situation in most Western countries.
It is this imbalance Nemtsov is tackling.

The average Russian electricity tariff for industry was 5.9 cents per kilowatt hour in May 1996 but just 1.4 cents per kilowatt hour for households. Industrial electricity prices in the United States and Britain average about 7 cents per kilowatt hour.
Average Russian tariffs were 45 percent lower than in the United States as of August 1996 and 90 percent lower than those in Germany, according to Troika.
